paper_metadata.title: Effect of low temperature on tensile properties of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy

evidence.quote: The effect of low temperature on tensile properties of a AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy (EHEA) was investigated in the present work.
The EHEA AlCoCrFeNi2.1 was prepared using arc-melting in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere starting with high purity elements (≥99.9%).
Figure 2 (a) shows a TEM image of the as-cast sample. A lamellar microstructure composed of two phases having different contrasts can be observed.

The EHEA AlCoCrFeNi2.1 was prepared using arc-melting in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere starting with high purity elements (≥99.9%). In order to ensure high level of chemical homogeneity, the melting process was repeated for at least five times.
The melt was drop-cast into a copper mold with dimensions of 15 mm (width) x 90 mm (length) x 3 mm (thickness).

It was confirmed that the dark phase with a thickness of ~600 nm marked by a filled green circle in Figure 2(a) was an ordered FCC- L1 2 phase showing extra superlattice reflections (marked by red circles in Figure 2(b)).

One interesting feature observed was that interfaces between the FCC and B2 phases are not sharp but diffused and decorated by dislocations, as indicated by the orange arrow in Figure 4(a).

the present TEM investigation of the specimen tensile tested at -196˚C shows dislocation activities not only in the FCC phase but also in the harder B2 phase (Figure 4(d)-(e)).

These results conclude that both soft FCC phase and hard B2 phase constructing the nano lamellar structure in the present HEA are plastically deformed and strain-hardened at -196˚C, which can be related to the higher strength of the present EHEA at -196˚C than that at room temperature, even when nano-twins are not formed.
Those results suggest that the disordering of L1 2 phase during the tensile deformation improves the ductility of the HEA, resulting in the total elongation of 17% maintained even at -196˚C.

The high strength and large elongation at -196˚C of the present EHEA were considered to be attributed to the disordering of the L1 2 phase into a ductile disordered FCC phase and the strain-hardening of the hard B2 phase at low temperatures.
